module ActiveStorageAttachmentStorageTracking
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create :track_storage_addition
  end

  def delete
    if persisted?
      transaction do
        location = resolve_storage_location
        bytes = attachment_byte_size if location
        affected_rows = _delete_row

        if affected_rows > 0 && location && bytes
          Storage::Entry.record(
            account_id: location[:account_id],
            board_id: location[:board_id],
            record_type: record_type,
            record_id: record_id,
            blob_id: blob_id,
            delta: -bytes,
            operation: "detach"
          )
        end
      end
    end

    @destroyed = true
    @previously_new_record = false
    freeze
  end

  private
    def destroy_row
      location = resolve_storage_location
      bytes = attachment_byte_size if location
      affected_rows = super

      if affected_rows > 0 && location && bytes
        Storage::Entry.record(
          account_id: location[:account_id],
          board_id: location[:board_id],
          record_type: record_type,
          record_id: record_id,
          blob_id: blob_id,
          delta: -bytes,
          operation: "detach"
        )
      end

      affected_rows
    end

    def track_storage_addition
      if location = resolve_storage_location
        if bytes = attachment_byte_size
          Storage::Entry.record(
            account_id: location[:account_id],
            board_id: location[:board_id],
            record_type: record_type,
            record_id: record_id,
            blob_id: blob_id,
            delta: bytes,
            operation: "attach"
          )
        end
      end
    end

    def resolve_storage_location
      case [ record_type, name ]
      when [ "Card", "image" ]
        resolve_card_location(record_id, loaded_card: loaded_record)
      when [ "ActionText::RichText", "embeds" ]
        resolve_rich_text_location
      end
    end

    def resolve_rich_text_location
      rich_text = loaded_record
      rt_record_type, rt_record_id, rt_name = if rich_text
        [ rich_text.record_type, rich_text.record_id, rich_text.name ]
      else
        ActionText::RichText.where(id: record_id).pick(:record_type, :record_id, :name)
      end

      rt_owner = rich_text.record if rich_text&.association(:record)&.loaded?

      case [ rt_record_type, rt_name ]
      when [ "Board", "public_description" ]
        resolve_board_location(rt_record_id, loaded_board: rt_owner)
      when [ "Card", "description" ]
        resolve_card_location(rt_record_id, loaded_card: rt_owner)
      when [ "Comment", "body" ]
        resolve_comment_location(rt_record_id, loaded_comment: rt_owner)
      end
    end

    def resolve_board_location(board_id, loaded_board: nil)
      return nil if board_id.blank? || Storage.destroying_board?(board_id)

      att_account_id = loaded_board&.account_id || account_id || Board.where(id: board_id).pick(:account_id)

      if att_account_id && !Storage.destroying_account?(att_account_id)
        { account_id: att_account_id, board_id: board_id }
      end
    end

    def resolve_card_location(card_id, loaded_card: nil)
      return nil if card_id.blank? || Storage.destroying_card?(card_id)

      att_account_id, board_id = if loaded_card
        [ loaded_card.account_id, loaded_card.board_id ]
      else
        Card.where(id: card_id).pick(:account_id, :board_id)
      end

      if att_account_id && board_id && !Storage.destroying_account?(att_account_id) && !Storage.destroying_board?(board_id)
        { account_id: att_account_id, board_id: board_id }
      end
    end

    def resolve_comment_location(comment_id, loaded_comment: nil)
      return nil if comment_id.blank?

      if loaded_comment
        loaded_card = loaded_comment.card if loaded_comment.association(:card).loaded?
        resolve_card_location(loaded_comment.card_id, loaded_card: loaded_card)
      else
        card_id = Comment.where(id: comment_id).pick(:card_id)
        resolve_card_location(card_id)
      end
    end

    def loaded_record
      record if association(:record).loaded?
    end

    def attachment_byte_size
      if association(:blob).loaded? && blob
        blob.byte_size
      else
        ActiveStorage::Blob.where(id: blob_id).pick(:byte_size)
      end
    end
end

messages.content: Let's create `test/models/storage_test.rb`, `test/jobs/storage/materialize_job_test.rb`, `test/jobs/storage/reconcile_job_test.rb`, and add storage assertions to `test/models/account/incineratable_test.rb` and `test/models/account/import_test.rb`.
messages.thinking:
**Comprehensive Storage Testing Strategy**

Okay, here's the plan. Looking at the test organization, it seems we're following a clear pattern, like we see in `test/models/storage_test.rb` and `test/models/search_test.rb`. We've got modular tests with some overlap. I see some more thorough test files like `test/models/board/storable_test.rb` and `test/models/account/storable_test.rb`. I'm thinking we can go even further, and build out a robust system across multiple test files.

We're going to dive deep and construct the following:

1.  `test/models/storage_test.rb`: This will be our central hub. It's going to be a comprehensive end-to-end test suite that covers every permutation of storage tracking across `Account` and `Board`. I want to validate every attachment type, ensure excluded types are handled correctly, and cover all the operations: variants, edits, replacements, clears, purges, detaches, card moves, simultaneous move+attachment edits, card destruction, board destruction. I'm also going to test unmaterialized and materialized combinations, rolled-back transactions, nested savepoint rollbacks, preloading to ensure all the include statements are working correctly, and multi-account isolation. This should give us airtight confidence in the model's storage logic.

2.  `test/jobs/storage/materialize_job_test.rb`: This job needs a dedicated test suite. I'm thinking we should address transaction coalescing (making sure one job is created for each transaction, even if many attachments are involved). We need to test batching across the `MATERIALIZE_BATCH_SIZE`, `ActiveJob::Continuable` checkpointing, and idempotency. Plus, we've got to make sure it handles being discarded when an account is deleted.

3.  `test/jobs/storage/reconcile_job_test.rb`: This will cover reconciling pre-existing or bulk-inserted attachments across boards. We'll need to handle concurrent new entries during the reconciliation and ensure that `ActiveJob::Continuable` cursor resumption works flawlessly.

4.  `test/models/account/incineratable_test.rb` & `test/models/account/import_test.rb`: We need to verify that our storage records are being cleaned up correctly during incineration and reconciled during export/import, so these files will be updated.

Time to write these tests and give them a good run!

**Debugging Two Test Failures: A Deep Dive**

Okay, this is interesting. I've got two distinct test setup issues here, and neither points directly to a bug in our core storage code. That's good, but let's see how they're set up.

First, that `Identity` class: it looks like it doesn't have an `account` method, which is a key clue. I remember `Identity` is global, and `ActiveStorage::Attachment.belongs_to :account` has a default value defined. Now, the `Identity#avatar` method is clearly not being used without an account, or it is a legacy usage. So, the question is, how is the avatar functionality tested in relation to the `Identity` model? I'll run `grep -rn "avatar" app/ test/` to get a quick overview of avatar usage in the tests. This should point out if the setup is misconfigured.

Now, the second error is a bit more involved. The key here seems to be the order of operations and how we're using ActiveJob. When `@card.comments.create!(...)` runs, the `Comment::Eventable` module kicks off `NotifyRecipientsJob`, which, in turn, creates a `Notification` and enqueues `Notification::PushJob(notification)`. The crucial point is that `Notification::PushJob` *doesn't* have `discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError`. Then, here's the kicker: `perform_enqueued_jobs` in Rails only processes jobs that are *currently* in `enqueued_jobs`, which means just the first wave. It doesn't recursively drain jobs enqueued *by* other jobs (unless called again or we specify `only: Storage::MaterializeJob`). So, `Notification::PushJob` is left hanging in `enqueued_jobs`. Then the `comment.destroy!` and `@card.destroy!` calls destroy the `Notification` object. Boom! On the *next* `perform_enqueued_jobs` call, `Notification::PushJob` tries to deserialize the destroyed `Notification` and throws a `DeserializationError`.

The workaround? Well, using `perform_enqueued_jobs only: Storage::MaterializeJob` in the test or draining jobs twice should prevent `Notification::PushJob` from failing because its `Notification` will be present. I should confirm this, just to be sure.

Alright, let's now check `test/models/identity_test.rb` and `test/controllers/cards/images_controller_test.rb` for how these are tested.

messages.content:
We have implemented background-materialized storage tracking with `#bytes_used` on both `Account` and `Board`.

### Summary of Changes

1. **Append-Only Delta Ledger + Materialized Totals (`Storage::Entry`, `Storage::Total`, `Storage::Totaled`)**:
   - Added `storage_entries` and `storage_totals` tables (`db/migrate/20260710120000_create_storage_tables.rb`, `db/schema.rb`, `db/schema_sqlite.rb`).
   - Foreground writes record lock-free, transactional delta entries (`Storage::Entry`) without updating `accounts` or `boards` rows directly, avoiding hot-row lock contention under heavy concurrent user activity.
   - Multiple attachment changes within a single transaction coalesce into a single `Storage::MaterializeJob` enqueued on commit.
   - `Account#bytes_used` and `Board#bytes_used` perform fast O(1) lookups against `storage_totals` (with preloading support via `includes(:storage_total)` and zero writes on read).

2. **Background Materialization & Reconciliation (`Account::Storable`, `Storage::MaterializeJob`, `Storage::ReconcileJob`)**:
   - `Storage::MaterializeJob` (with `ActiveJob::Continuable`) drains pending `storage_entries` in batches under a short lock on the account's `Storage::Total`, updating affected board totals and the account total in O(pending deltas) time regardless of total attachment count.
   - `Storage::ReconcileJob` (triggered automatically after `Account::Import#process`) reconciles storage across boards when records are bulk-imported via `insert_all!`.

3. **Exact Attachment Scope & Lifecycle Tracking (`ActiveStorageAttachmentStorageTracking`, `Board::Storable`, `Card::Storable`, `Comment::Storable`)**:
   - Counts only `Card#image` attachments and files embedded (`ActionText::RichText#embeds`) in `Board#public_description`, `Card#description`, and `Comment#body` (ignoring variants, avatars, exports/imports, unattached blobs, mentions, and remote media).
   - Tracks additions, replacements, rich-text edits/clears (`config/initializers/action_text.rb`), `destroy`, `purge`, `purge_later`, and `detach`.
   - Transfers counted storage across boards on card or comment moves, and collapses card/board/account destructions cleanly without per-attachment query storms.
